# Finance baseline and value-measurement plan

**SYNTHETIC - NOT CLIENT-ATTESTED.** No Finance-approved baseline, rate card,
funding decision, savings, or ROI is included in this file.

## Current evidence status

- Finance owner: not identified in this synthetic scenario.
- HR reporting labor baseline: not supplied.
- Existing platform/license cost: not supplied.
- Current report production effort and defect/rework rate: not measured.
- Cost of proposed delivery: to be estimated from scoped work packages,
  delivery model, role mix, rate assumptions, and human-review effort.
- Benefit realization: not claimed. Any productivity or decision-quality benefit
  requires an agreed baseline, counterfactual, adoption measure, and Finance
  sign-off.

## Transparent model to use later

1. Separate one-time implementation effort from recurring platform, support,
   and report-maintenance cost.
2. Estimate low/base/high hours by work package and role. Label every value as
   either sourced, a planning assumption, or pending confirmation.
3. Compare internal and vendor delivery on the same scope and acceptance
   criteria; disclose rate source, overhead treatment, and excluded costs.
4. If Claude Code or Codex are assumed to accelerate implementation, show the
   eligible tasks, assumed productivity factor, retained human-review hours,
   and net hours separately. Do not reduce test, security, privacy, or business
   review to zero.
5. Keep benefits at zero/unquantified until Finance supplies and approves a
   defensible baseline. Do not multiply assumed hours by a made-up labor cost
   and call it savings.

## Required Finance inputs before a business case can be final

- Current report preparation and reconciliation time by role, with source and
  representative period.
- Current platform, connector, and license charges allocated to the use case.
- Approved internal planning rates and vendor proposal/rate card.
- Recurring support/maintenance owner and cost assumptions.
- Finance-approved benefit formula, counterfactual, measurement period, and
  realization owner.

This item is intentionally sufficient to expose a missing baseline, not to
manufacture one. The app must preserve that distinction in generated outputs.
